title: Duel Decks: Elves vs. Inventors: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Great hero or grand betrayer? The truth of Ezuri's legacy is clouded by the fog of legend.
"This is our land. We will not allow eyeblights to poison its beauty."
Call one, call them all.
"The elves tend the forest, and the forest sustains the elves. My role is to ensure that the cycle continues."
"How do the vinebred feel? Fah! We do not ask the puppet how it feels when the puppeteer bids it dance."
"Life grows everywhere. My kin merely find those places where it grows strongest." —Nissa Revane
"Our lives are woven together like the trees' branches over our heads, forming a canopy that protects us all."
Eyes and arrows trained ever skyward.
"Skyknight gear? Well, I have drake-skin gauntlets, supple and fireproof. Or a ceratok chestplate that'll stop a crossbow bolt."
Every leaf, tree, and building in Kujar has been placed to achieve maximum harmony, in accordance with the elvish philosophy known as the Great Conduit.
Eidren, perfect of Lys Alana, ordered hundreds of trees uprooted and rearranged into a pattern he deemed beautiful. Thus the Gilt-Leaf Wood was born.
The remains of ancient civilizations litter the run-down land.
Many elves incorporate the beauty of nature into their inventions. Very few capture its savagery.
It rarely moves, standing stock still in its clearing. When it does stir, ravens stop their cawing and crickets their chirping. All of nature watches in awed silence.
"The land gives of itself. Its abundance provides, even in times of chaos."
The safewright Talara protects a delicate woodland waterfall. She has vowed to send wave after wave of warriors to slay any who would dare disturb its beauty.
She stands as a living symbol of the natural world and an enemy of the forces that threaten it.
"Life as we know it dangles on the brink of extinction. We must show the strength they would steal from us." —*The Invokers' Tales*
"I can call an army to my side in the blink of an eye. Best not blink."
The artificers of Kaladesh strive ceaselessly for perfection, progress, and the ultimate expression of elegance.
The greatest masters of the craft abandon tools altogether, shaping metal with hand and mind alone.
The Neurok see the artificer as an archaeologist, clearing away falsehoods to see the truth hidden beneath.
"The tools of the past will help us forge the future."
The elves had devised countless strategies to combat Memnarch's war machines, but they had no idea what to do when one was *thrown* at them.
The metal must be pure. The hand must be steady. The product must be perfect.
From trinket to trauma.
"The fires of invention burn in all of us. I fight for the freedom to unleash those flames." —Pia Nalaar
It's not wise to disturb an artist at work.
"If there can be no victory, then I will fight forever." —Koth of the Hammer
"It's the must-have gift for everyone on your list. Get one for yourself, too!" —Chammi, curio vendor
"Our glorious infection has taken hold." —Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite
The oil created the mycosynth. The mycosynth created New Phyrexia.
For the Phyrexians, death is not an end, nor a one-time occurrence.
All the curiosity of the Neurok with only a trace of their duplicity.
"Melt that which was never frozen." —Spellbomb inscription
A masterwork of spite, inspired by madness.
Voyager staffs are sought by those hoping to find an escape from the sprawling glut of Ravnica.
Structures built from darksteel yield to neither assault nor age.
All around the foundry, automatons unhitched themselves from their mounts and pivoted to face Chandra.
Kuldotha, wellspring of molten metal, temple of the goblin horde.
"So even the heart of our world has succumbed." —Koth of the Hammer
Lumengrid, site of the Knowledge Pool, source of vedalken arcana.
